subject: aptitude
title_en: Time & Work Part 2 — Joining & Leaving, Group Work, Wages & Alternate Days
title_ta: காலம் மற்றும் வேலை பகுதி 2 — சேருதல்/விலகுதல், குழு வேலை, கூலி பகிர்வு மற்றும் மாற்று நாட்கள்

definition.en: Part 2 covers partial work scenarios where workers join or leave mid-way, group work equations involving men and women, wage division based on work contribution, and alternate day rotation schedules.
definition.ta: பகுதி 2-ல் இடையில் சேருதல் அல்லது விலகுதல் கணக்குகள், ஆண்கள் மற்றும் பெண்கள் சேர்ந்த குழு வேலை, வேலைப் பங்கிற்கு ஏற்ப கூலி பிரித்தளித்தல் மற்றும் மாற்று நாட்களில் வேலை செய்யும் கணக்குகள் ஆகியவை அடங்கும்.

exam_importance.en: Part 2 covers high-yield TNPSC Group 1 and Group 2/2A standard questions. Topics such as A leaving mid-way, men vs women equivalent efficiency, wage distribution proportional to work done, and alternate day work cycles are frequently tested.
exam_importance.ta: பகுதி 2-ல் TNPSC குரூப் 1 மற்றும் குரூப் 2/2A தேர்வுகளில் கேட்கப்படும் அதிக வினாக்கள் இடம்பெற்றுள்ளன. ஒருவர் இடையில் விலகுதல், ஆண்-பெண் சமமான வேலைத்திறன், கூலிப் பகிர்வு மற்றும் மாற்று நாள் கணக்குகள் இதில் அடங்கும்.

explanation.en: Calculate the work units finished during the first period, subtract from total work, then calculate time for remaining work.
explanation.ta: முதல் கட்டத்தில் முடிந்த வேலையைக் கணக்கிட்டு, மீதமுள்ள வேலையைத் தனியாகத் தீர்க்க வேண்டும்.

formula_sheet.title: Wage Distribution Rule (கூலிப் பகிர்வு விதி)
formula_sheet.formula: Wage_A : Wage_B = \text{Work Done by A} : \text{Work Done by B}

explanation.en: Wages are distributed strictly proportional to the fraction of work completed by each individual (or 1-day work rates if working for equal days).
explanation.ta: ஒவ்வொருவரும் செய்து முடித்த வேலைப் பங்கின் விகிதத்திலேயே கூலி பிரிக்கப்படும்.

formula_sheet.title: Alternate Day Cycle Formula (மாற்று நாள் சுழற்சி சூத்திரம்)
formula_sheet.formula: 1 \text{ Cycle (2 Days)} = A\text{'s 1-day work} + B\text{'s 1-day work}

explanation.en: Find work done in one 2-day cycle, determine total complete cycles needed, and solve for any remaining fraction.
explanation.ta: ஒரு சுழற்சிக்கான (2 நாட்கள்) வேலையைக் கணக்கிட்டு, எத்தனை சுழற்சிகள் தேவை என்பதைத் தீர்மானித்தல்.

core_concepts.title: Men, Women & Boys Equivalent Work Logic (ஆண்கள், பெண்கள் சமச்சீர் வேலை)

en: Equate work equations: (m1 Men + w1 Women) × D1 = (m2 Men + w2 Women) × D2.
Solve for the efficiency relation: x Men = y Women (e.g. 1 Man = 2 Women).
Convert the entire target workforce into a single unit type (all Men or all Women) to apply simple chain rule.
ta: வேலை சமன்பாடுகளைச் சமப்படுத்துக: (m1 ஆண்கள் + w1 பெண்கள்) × D1 = (m2 ஆண்கள் + w2 பெண்கள்) × D2.
திறன் தொடர்பைக் கண்டறிக: x ஆண்கள் = y பெண்கள் (எ.கா. 1 ஆண் = 2 பெண்கள்).
கேட்கப்பட்ட ஆட்களை ஒரே பிரிவாக (அனைத்தும் ஆண்கள் அல்லது அனைத்தும் பெண்கள்) மாற்றி சங்கிலிச் சூத்திரத்தைப் பயன்படுத்தவும்.

en: If all workers work for the same total number of days: Wages are divided in the ratio of their 1-day work rates.
Ratio of Wages A : B = (1 / A) : (1 / B) = B : A.
ta: அனைத்து தொழிலாளர்களும் ஒரே எண்ணிக்கையிலான நாட்கள் வேலை செய்தால்: கூலியானது அவர்களின் 1 நாள் வேலை விகிதத்தில் (திறன் விகிதத்தில்) பிரிக்கப்படும்.

exam_traps.trap: Dividing wages in ratio of days instead of efficiency/work done

explanation.en: If A takes 6 days and B takes 12 days, dividing wages as 6 : 12 = 1 : 2 is WRONG! A is faster, so A gets more money (ratio 12 : 6 = 2 : 1).
explanation.ta: A 6 நாட்கள், B 12 நாட்கள் எனில் கூலியை 6 : 12 எனப் பிரிப்பது தவறாகும்! A வேகமானவர் என்பதால் A-க்கே அதிக கூலி கிடைக்கும் (விகிதம் 12 : 6 = 2 : 1).

avoidance.en: Wages ratio is INVERSE to days ratio when working equal days: Wage A : Wage B = 1/6 : 1/12 = 2 : 1.
avoidance.ta: கூலி விகிதம் நாட்களின் விகிதத்திற்கு எதிர்ப்பிகிதத்தில் அமையும்: கூலி A : B = 2 : 1.

solved_examples.question: A can do a piece of work in 20 days and B in 30 days. A works alone for 5 days and then leaves. In how many days can B finish the remaining work?
steps: Step 1: Total Work = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units.
Step 2: Daily rates: A = \(60 / 20 = 3\) units/day; B = \(60 / 30 = 2\) units/day.
Step 3: Work completed by A in 5 days = \(5 \times 3 = 15\) units.
Step 4: Remaining Work = \(60 - 15 = 45\) units.
Step 5: Time taken by B for remaining work = \(\frac{45}{2} = 22.5\) days (or \(22 \frac{1}{2}\) days).

solved_examples.question: If 4 men can complete a work in 3 days and 3 women can complete that work in 6 days, can 6 men and 8 women complete the work in one day?
steps: Step 1: 4 Men in 3 days \(\implies\) 1 Man's 1-day work = \(\frac{1}{4 \times 3} = \frac{1}{12}\).
Step 2: 3 Women in 6 days \(\implies\) 1 Woman's 1-day work = \(\frac{1}{3 \times 6} = \frac{1}{18}\).
Step 3: Calculate 1-day work of 6 Men + 8 Women: \(6 \times \frac{1}{12} + 8 \times \frac{1}{18} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{4}{9} = \frac{9 + 8}{18} = \frac{17}{18}\).
Step 4: Since \(\frac{17}{18} \neq 1\), they complete only 17/18 of the work in one day. So it is NOT complete.
solved_examples.answer: No, they finish 17/18 of the work in 1 day (incomplete)

solved_examples.question: A and B undertake to do a piece of work for ₹1,200. A alone can do it in 8 days and B alone in 12 days. With the help of C, they finish it in 4 days. Find C's share of the wages.
steps: Step 1: Combined rate of A, B, C = \(\frac{1}{4}\). A's rate = \(\frac{1}{8}\), B's rate = \(\frac{1}{12}\).
Step 3: Ratio of 1-day work A : B : C = \(\frac{1}{8} : \frac{1}{12} : \frac{1}{24} = 3 : 2 : 1\).
Step 4: Total ratio parts = 3 + 2 + 1 = 6 parts.
Step 5: C's share = \(\frac{1}{6} \times 1200 = ₹200\).

solved_examples.question: A can do a work in 10 days and B in 15 days. If they work on alternate days starting with A, in how many days will the work be completed?
steps: Step 1: Total Work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units.
Step 2: Daily rates: A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day.
Step 3: Work done in 1 cycle (2 days) = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Step 4: Number of 2-day cycles needed = \(30 / 5 = 6\) cycles.
Step 5: Total days = \(6 \times 2 = 12\) days.

solved_examples.question: A and B can do a work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They worked together for 4 days, then A left. How many more days will B take to finish the remaining work?
steps: Step 1: Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.
Step 2: Daily rates: A = 3 units/day, B = 2 units/day.
Step 3: Combined 1-day work = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
Step 4: Work done together in 4 days = \(4 \times 5 = 20\) units.
Step 5: Remaining Work = \(36 - 20 = 16\) units.
Step 6: Time taken by B alone = \(\frac{16}{2} = 8\) days.

solved_examples.question: 2 men and 3 boys can do a piece of work in 10 days, while 3 men and 2 boys can do the same work in 8 days. In how many days can 2 men and 1 boy do the work?
steps: Step 1: Write work equivalence equation: \((2M + 3B) \times 10 = (3M + 2B) \times 8\).
Step 2: Expand: \(20M + 30B = 24M + 16B \implies 4M = 14B \implies 2M = 7B\) (1 Man = 3.5 Boys).
Step 3: Convert 1st team to Boys: \(2M + 3B = 7B + 3B = 10\) Boys. 10 Boys take 10 days \(\implies\) Total Work = 100 Boy-days.
Step 4: Convert target team to Boys: \(2M + 1B = 7B + 1B = 8\) Boys.
Step 5: Time for 8 Boys = \(\frac{100}{8} = 12.5\) days.

practice_questions.question: A takes 12 days and B takes 24 days. A works alone for 3 days and leaves. How many days will B take to finish the remaining work?
practice_questions.explanation: Total Work = 24 units. A rate = 2, B rate = 1. A in 3 days = 6 units. Rem = 18 units. B takes 18/1 = 18 days.

practice_questions.question: A, B, and C undertake a work for ₹600. A takes 6 days, B takes 8 days, C takes 12 days. Find B's share of wages.
A can do a work in 6 days and B in 12 days. They work on alternate days starting with A. In how many days is it finished?
practice_questions.explanation: LCM = 12 units. A=2, B=1. 2-day cycle = 3 units. 4 cycles = 8 days.

practice_questions.question: 3 men or 6 women can do a work in 20 days. How many days will 1 man and 2 women take to complete it?
A and B together can do a work in 10 days. They work together for 4 days, then B leaves. A finishes remaining work in 9 days. How many days for A alone?
practice_questions.explanation: 4 days combined work = 4/10 = 2/5. Remaining work = 3/5. A takes 9 days for 3/5 ⇒ A alone = 9 × (5/3) = 15 days.

quick_revision_cards.back: Calculate completed work fraction ⇒ Remaining Work = 1 - Completed Work
Wages are divided in exact proportion to work done by each person
1 Cycle (2 days) = Work A + Work B ⇒ Total Days = Cycles × 2
Equate (M1 × D1 = M2 × D2) ⇒ Find 1 Man = x Women ratio
Wage A : Wage B = 1/Days_A : 1/Days_B = Days_B : Days_A
